scoring_justification: Stability pattern is structural audit; formation and binding energy ranges are recomputed from agent's raw energies_summary.csv and compared to paper-reported intervals with tolerances.

outputs.description: Per-configuration stability classification across charge states. Checker verifies structural trend: all 9 configurations stable at +2, progressively fewer at 0 (only the three largest remain stable), only the largest (~8.1 Å) stable at -2.

schema.notes: config_id and charge_state are nullable for isolated defects; formation_energy_eV and binding_energy_eV are nullable for isolated defects.

outputs.description: Formation and binding energies for stable Frenkel pairs (one row per stable configuration per charge state) and for isolated vacancy and interstitial. Checker extracts min/max formation energy range and min/max binding energy range and checks they fall within the paper's reported ranges with tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The stability table reports the classification from the geometry relaxations. The energies summary reports the computed formation and binding energies. Both files are required; the checker verifies the stability trend and energy ranges against the paper's reported values.

hidden_assets.purpose: expected stability pattern and energy range tolerance bounds
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Fig. 6 and section III.B text: stability pattern and energy ranges
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted from paper description; reference solve.sh hardcodes values that match the paper exactly
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: derived from paper's reported stability dependence and formation/binding energy ranges; tolerances chosen to account for DFT code variation.

steps.description: Verify stability pattern: +2: all 9 stable; 0: only configs 7,8,9 stable; -2: only config 9 stable.

Compute min and max formation energy among stable FP rows; must fall within [5.80, 6.85] eV. Compute min and max binding energy; must fall within [0.16, 1.11] eV. Partial credit for degradation beyond tolerance.
